rationale: Pedigree cosegregation analyses and recessive disease cohorts demonstrate that monoallelic carrier relatives of probands with biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function (LoF) variants do not exhibit the classical dominant CADASIL phenotype; they do not develop premature recurrent strokes, early vascular dementia, or vascular NOTCH3 extracellular domain (Notch3ECD) accumulation, and large population-level biobank data (UK Biobank) confirm that monoallelic LoF variants do not confer an increased stroke risk over population controls. However, the hypothesis that monoallelic LoF variants lack vascular pathogenicity is challenged by clinical and radiological registry data: clinically ascertained monoallelic LoF carriers exhibit stroke in 15% (11/69) and subcortical lacunar infarcts in 38% (12/32), accompanied by white matter hyperintensity volumes (nWMHv) and diffusion alterations (PSMD) that are quantitatively comparable to pathogenic CADASIL cysteine-altering variants. Thus, while dominant classic CADASIL pathogenicity (driven by Notch3ECD aggregation) is absent, monoallelic LoF variants may confer a milder, variable-penetrance small vessel disease phenotype later in life.

evidence.text: In a systematic cohort of 50 patients with biallelic NOTCH3 variants (26 with loss-of-function variants), monoallelic LoF carriers were predominantly asymptomatic, with only a small minority reporting nonspecific headaches.

evidence.text: Pedigree analysis of a homozygous NOTCH3 null variant proband confirmed that consanguineous heterozygous parents and three unrelated individuals with incidental heterozygous NOTCH3 null variants did not manifest CADASIL phenotypes.

In addition, three heterozygous NOTCH3 null variants were reported as incidental findings in three unrelated cases analyzed in our center.

Only the carriers of the cysteine-altering variant demonstrated NOTCH3 extracellular domain (NOTCH3 ECD ) immunoreactivity in skin vessels.

evidence.text: Recent pathobiological research demonstrates that CADASIL pathogenesis is primarily driven by NOTCH3 extracellular domain (Notch3ECD) multimerization and aggregation rather than loss-of-function, explaining the distinct mechanism of recessive biallelic LoF disorders.

source.quote: Recent research has challenged the loss-of-function hypothesis, instead implicating Notch3ECD aggregation, involving both mutant and wild-type NOTCH3, as the primary driver of vascular pathology in CADASIL.

evidence.text: In UK Biobank, 102 monoallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function carriers exhibited increased white matter hyperintensity volume and PSMD comparable to CADASIL cysteine carriers, though without increased stroke risk; however, in clinically ascertained monoallelic LoF cases, stroke was present in 15% and lacunes in 38%.

conflicts: Clinical ascertainment reveals stroke in 15% (11/69) and lacunes in 38% (12/32) of monoallelic NOTCH3 LoF variant carriers (Neurology, DOI:10.1212/WNL.0000000000214021), directly contradicting the assumption that monoallelic LoF variants never cause ischemic strokes.

Population neuroimaging in UK Biobank shows that monoallelic NOTCH3 LoF carriers develop white matter hyperintensity loads (Δ0.44 mm3, p < 0.001) and microstructural white matter injury (PSMD Δ0.19 × 10-4, p = 0.017) comparable in magnitude to pathogenic CADASIL cysteine-altering variants, conflicting with the claim that monoallelic LoF status is entirely benign or non-penetrant.

new_directions.question_text: To what extent do shared vascular risk factors (e.g., hypertension, smoking) account for the 15% stroke rate observed in clinically ascertained monoallelic NOTCH3 LoF cases versus unselected population biobank carriers?
new_directions.rationale: Determining whether strokes in monoallelic LoF carriers represent CADASIL-mimicking arteriopathy versus classic hypertensive small vessel disease is critical for genetic counseling and stroke prevention guidelines.

new_directions.question_text: Does haploinsufficiency of NOTCH3 alter cerebral blood flow autoregulation or mural cell coverage in the microvasculature without inducing Notch3ECD aggregation?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the functional microvascular consequences of reduced NOTCH3 dosage will establish whether LoF variants cause a distinct non-aggregating arteriopathy responsible for subclinical white matter hyperintensities.
